sources.title: Constitution of Tonga, 2020 Revised Edition
sources.publisher: Attorney General's Office, Tonga

claims.text: Clauses 30 and 41 describe a constitutional monarchy; royal signature is required for legislation. Clause 36 assigns military command to the King but requires Assembly consent for war.

The King appoints the Assembly-recommended elected representative as prime minister. Cabinet exercises executive authority collectively and answers to the Assembly; ministers are nominated by the prime minister and appointed by the King. Reserved royal powers are excluded.
The King appoints Privy Council advisers. The Council also handles specified hereditary estate and title appeals.
The Assembly includes nobles' representatives, people's representatives and Cabinet. Its recommended Speaker must be an elected nobles' representative and is appointed by the King.

Clause 32 of the 2020 Revised Edition sets hereditary succession to the Crown and Throne: to the eldest male child and the heirs of his body, through the male line, then to the female line, with fallback procedures if there is no lawful heir.
claims.uncertainty: A legal rule in a consolidated edition. It dates no accession and is not backdated to 1990. Re-read on 2026-09-21 for CLAUDE-C01-07; the source's recorded access date is that of its first intake. Downloaded copy: 789,048 bytes, SHA-256 197f1dcaf64c3267e589354aafdc2783dae7fac9f4d3b296808d21d45f7004de.

claims.text: Clause 34 prescribes the oath to be taken by those who succeed to the throne. The clause does not make succession conditional on the oath, and it does not fix when the oath is taken.
claims.uncertainty: No coronation-oath event is dated by this clause, and no retrieved source dates the oath for George Tupou V or Tupou VI. Re-read on 2026-09-21 for CLAUDE-C01-07; the source's recorded access date is that of its first intake.

claims.text: Clause 43 provides: 'Should the King wish to travel abroad it shall be lawful for him to appoint a Prince Regent who shall administer the affairs of the Kingdom during his absence.' If the King dies while his heir is under eighteen and his will names no Prince Regent, the Legislative Assembly 'shall choose by ballot a Prince Regent', 'but the representatives of the people shall have no voice in such election'. Clause 42 refers a minority regency to clause 43.
claims.uncertainty: Enabling provision only; it records no appointment. A regent administers the Kingdom during the King's absence or the heir's minority and is not a King. Re-read on 2026-09-21 for CLAUDE-C01-07; the source's recorded access date is that of its first intake.

sources.scope_note: Consolidated edition, not a complete amendment or commencement ledger. Do not backdate these provisions to 1990 or assume no later amendments.

roles.title: King

holder_claims.name: Taufa'ahau Tupou IV
holder_claims.note: King when the period opens: dated royal assents of 12 July and 8 August 1990 (TO-CROWN-01). His reign ended with his death in Auckland at 00:34 on 11 September 2006, Tongan time (23:34 on 10 September, New Zealand time), as Gazette No. 20 records; Gazette No. 19 states that the Crown devolved by his decease (TO-CROWN-03, TO-CROWN-04).
holder_claims.uncertainty: The start of the reign (1965) is outside the period and is not structured. The end is the Tongan calendar date of the death, to which the proclamation's devolution wording ties the transfer of the Crown; it is not taken from George Tupou V's proclamation or coronation. The State Funeral, burial and mourning are separate claims.

holder_claims.name: George Tupou V
holder_claims.note: Formerly Crown Prince Tupouto'a; Siaosi Tupou V in the Tongan texts. Accession by devolution of the Crown on the decease of Taufa'ahau Tupou IV at 00:34 on 11 September 2006, Tongan time (TO-CROWN-04); proclaimed King by Gazette No. 19 on the same Tongan day, as a separate event. Traditional installation (taumafa kava) on 30 July 2008 and coronation on 1 August 2008 (TO-CROWN-05). Died in Hong Kong at 20:58 on 18 March 2012, Tonga time (TO-CROWN-06).
holder_claims.uncertainty: The start is the stated devolution on his predecessor's death, not the proclamation, the traditional installation, the coronation or the coronation oath (which no source dates). The end is his death as Gazette Extraordinary No. 8 records it; Gazette Extraordinary No. 9 states that the Crown devolved by his decease. No accession time is stored.

holder_claims.name: Tupou VI
holder_claims.note: Formerly Crown Prince Tupouto'a Lavaka, the former Prince 'Ulukalala Lavaka Ata, on whom the Crown Prince title was vested in September 2006. Accession by devolution of the Crown on the decease of George Tupou V at 20:58 on 18 March 2012, Tonga time; proclaimed King on 19 March 2012 as a separate event (TO-CROWN-07); crowned on 4 July 2015 (TO-CROWN-08).
holder_claims.uncertainty: The start is the stated devolution on his predecessor's death, not the proclamation or the coronation. No end is inferred: no source here records one before the 7 September 2026 cutoff, and the latest attestation in this packet is 18 December 2025 (to_tupou_vi_2025).
